contract: Exact currency amounts over a closed, versioned ISO 4217 registry folded append-only from a dated, source-attributed derived extract (current list 2026-09-17, historic list 2026-01-01): a currency is a registry member with alpha code, numeric code or explicit absence, and minor-unit exponent or explicit :not_applicable/:not_recorded, plus its status and registry version; an amount is an integer count of minor units scaled by that exponent. Pure Cure same-currency add/subtract/compare/negate and ratio allocation (1..1000 non-negative integer ratios, positive sum, shares truncated toward zero, residual placed :first/:last/:spread on positive-ratio parts and reported as already placed); untrusted alpha/numeric parse distinguishes malformed from unknown; version-specific membership on every call (forged_currency); exact Decimal-string and %Decimal{} boundaries with declared rounding modes; canonical versioned codec bytes that decode to the original identity after registry updates. Typed rejections: currency_mismatch, unknown_currency, malformed_code, retired_currency, scale_overflow, malformed_amount, invalid_ratios, unknown_rounding_mode, unknown_placement, no_minor_unit, forged_currency, unknown_registry_version. No Float.
limits: No exchange rates, locale formatting, journal posting, payment provider or usage-unit semantics; whether a posting context accepts a retired currency is domain/journal's decision.

The allocation sum (parts sum to the total), the residual bound and every Elixir boundary are finite tests, not proofs: pinned Cure 20824806 keeps native Int + and Std.Builtin.struct_eq neutral on symbolic values, and Std.Proof.IntOrder has no runtime module, so arithmetic laws take the currency and ratio-validity decisions as evidence (decision-split form). A test records that a dropped-residual copy still checks.

Registry coverage is the held extract only (ISO current list published 2026-09-17, historic list 2026-01-01, downloaded 2026-11-08); no claim that the registry is current afterwards. Identities absent from held versions are not reconstructed: codes retired before the first held version have minor unit :not_recorded and construct no amount.

The extract is derived from the SIX Group files (source URLs and SHA-256 in its header); no SIX file is committed. mix check compares the registry with the extract, not with the SIX files; fidelity rests on the recorded run of test/support/iso4217_derive_test_helper.exs --check. Redistribution terms for the extract were not verified; the main coordinator chose this option as a prudence decision reported to the owner; no legal conclusion is made.
numeric_candidates/2 is an enumeration, not a parse: historic numeric codes are reused and the Piece never chooses among them. parse_numeric/2 resolves only among codes active in the stated version.

Amounts are bounded: abs(minor units) < 10^38 at construction and after every add, subtract and rounding step (scale_overflow beyond it), so every accepted amount encodes within the codec's 128-byte decode limit. Decimal strings at most 40 bytes and 38 significant digits; %Decimal{} coefficient at most 38 digits and exponent -38..38; rounding scale -18..exponent. Conversion and rounding are integer arithmetic; the process Decimal context never applies.

Membership is checked in Elixir on every public call; calling Cure.Elzoo.Money directly bypasses it. Amounts of one alpha with different identities (for example after an exponent change) are different currencies.
Persistence is the caller's Store: Codec writes bytes and makes no storage, durability or delivery claim. The integration/sql round trip is a repository test, not part of this bundle.

grounding.claim: M1: for amounts left, right and a same-currency decision proved True, add_with returns MoneyOk of left's currency and units(left) + units(right) (decision-split form).
M2: with the same-currency decision proved False, add_with returns MoneyRejected(MoneyCurrencyMismatch(currency(left), currency(right))).
M3: with the decision True, subtract_with returns MoneyOk of left's currency and units(left) - units(right).
M4: with the decision False, subtract_with returns the mismatch naming left and right currencies.
M5: with the decision False, compare_with returns the mismatch naming left and right currencies.
M6: for every amount, negate keeps its currency (by reduction).
M7: with the ratio-validity decision proved False, allocate_with allocates nothing (MoneyAllocationRejected(MoneyInvalidRatios)).
M8: for every currency, total, ratio list and sum, shares has exactly one part per ratio (induction on ratios).
M9: every share carries the allocated currency (induction on ratios).
M10: residual placement keeps the part count for every placement, ratio list and remaining residual (induction on parts).
M11: residual placement keeps every part's currency (induction on parts).
M12: with the validity decision True, the production allocate_with has exactly one part per ratio for every placement.
M13: with the validity decision True, every part of the production allocation is in the total's currency.

Pinned Cure checks the MoneyCurrency, MoneyAmount, MoneyResult, MoneyComparison, MoneyAllocation and MoneyAllocationResult schema and the production arithmetic with a clean audit (no axioms, holes, unresolved, unaudited, opaque or unproven-total items; every function @total). Tests reject mutated copies at the named law: an extra part (distribute_count), a share in another currency (shares_currency), an add that keeps the right currency (add_same_currency), an add that ignores the mismatch and a swapped mismatch (add_mismatch_names_both).

Listed scenarios: exact EUR parts and residual per placement for eight totals and ratio lists including negative, zero-ratio and zero totals; JPY 1000 and BHD 1.234 allocations; bounded exhaustive allocation (totals -60..60, ratio lists of length 1..3 over 0..3, all placements: sum, count, zero-ratio parts, |part - share| <= |residual|, changed-part count) with a dropped-residual negative control; invalid ratios and placements; same-currency arithmetic and typed mismatch; a test-only C9 account fixture refusing a charge in another currency; exponent scaling for JPY, BHD, EUR, CLF, UYW with fixed-hundredth and Float negative controls; scale_overflow and malformed strings; 35..38-digit exact conversion and 39-digit rejection; every rounding mode for from_decimal and round, including a non-default caller Decimal context; malformed %Decimal{} structs; the declared amount range at 10^38 - 1 and 10^38 for construction, add, subtract, round and codec replay; Float and wrong-type rejection at every public function. Not universal proofs.

Listed scenarios over the committed extract read by an independent parser: header sources, dates and SHA-256; row counts (280 current, 169 historic, 178 active, 307 entries); every currency-bearing current row resolves by alpha and numeric to the same canonical value with its minor unit or N.A.; the 3 other current rows carry no fields; every historic row resolves by alpha with its numeric or absence and withdrawal text and appears in numeric_candidates; every entry has a source row; a synthetic next version (EUR removed, ISK exponent changed, numeric 191 reused, FIM omitted) retains entries and exponents, decodes old bytes to the original identity, and separates version-qualified numeric lookups, and gives a newly retired code a withdrawal only from historic rows unseen in earlier versions (else :not_recorded, kept across a three-version fold); an explicit version option is validated by every value function and the codec; a deleting fold is caught; version-specific forgery and non-canonical codec bytes are rejected. Not universal proofs.
Relies on the pinned Cure compiler, kernel, Std.Equivalent.trans and audit.

Relies on the Decimal 3.2.0 struct fields (sign, coef, exp), Decimal.new/3 exact construction and the rounding-mode names; Decimal arithmetic rounds to the process context and is not used for conversion. G3 comparison with ex_money 6.3.0 is recorded in docs/work/ELZ-031-sql-probe.md; ex_money behaviour is compared, not proved.
Relies on pinned Elixir/OTP integer arithmetic (div/rem truncation), Regex and binaries, and compile-time module attributes for the registry.

The SIX Group list files of 2026-09-17 and 2026-01-01 are the ISO 4217 maintenance agency's publications, and the committed extract equals the recorded derivation run on them; callers persist Codec bytes and the registry version they were resolved under.

telemetry.contract: Pure callable, no process; the invoking Unit or Assembly instruments. Results are caller values, not telemetry.

config.contract: Per call, no default for policy choices, no hot reconfiguration: rounding mode (one of :down, :half_up, :half_even, :ceiling, :floor, :half_down, :up), rounding scale (integer -18..exponent), allocation placement (:first | :last | :spread), allocation ratios (1..1000 non-negative integers, positive sum), and options registry: (a value from Elzoo.Money.Registry.build!/1, default the compiled registry) and version: (a held version id: selects the version for parse and parse_numeric, default the newest; limits numeric_candidates; for every function taking a currency, amount or codec bytes it must equal each value's version, else forged_currency; an unheld version is unknown_registry_version). The registry data is fixed per bundle revision and changes only by adding a dated extract.

control.contract: No lifecycle to pause, drain or resume.
